traditionalDress.men: An angarkha (a long overlapping tunic) or dhoti-kurta, paired with a colorful pagri (turban) whose style and color can indicate the wearer's region and community.
traditionalDress.women: A ghagra-choli (or lehenga-choli) — a long flared skirt with a fitted blouse — paired with an odhni (veil), often decorated with mirror work, embroidery, or bandhani (tie-dye) patterns.

festivals.name: Teej
festivals.description: A monsoon festival honoring Goddess Parvati, celebrated mainly by women who dress in green and take part in processions, especially grand in Jaipur.

festivals.name: Gangaur
festivals.description: A festival celebrating the union of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, marked by women carrying decorated idols of the goddess in colorful processions.

festivals.name: Jaisalmer Desert Festival
festivals.description: A winter festival in the Thar Desert featuring folk music, Kalbelia dance performances, camel events, and traditional crafts.

music: Sung with sarangi, algoza, and dholak
folklore: The Rajasthani folk ballad of Dhola and Maru is one of the region's oldest and most widely sung love legends: a prince and princess separated for years by distance and circumstance, whose devotion endures until they are eventually reunited — a story still performed by folk singers in Jaisalmer and Bikaner.
